what_this_is: The census of authority sites (self-proof execution plan, lane P, unit P1): every site in Clean's production Rust (crates/**/*.rs), and in one pinned Trust commit, that spells an authority-shaped acceptance in the scanned vocabulary (`limits` says what that vocabulary leaves out) or selects the checker behind one. It is the map for the later flip to kcheck; it changes no kernel behaviour and claims nothing about soundness. scripts/check_authority_sites.py re-derives the site list from source and fails when a site in that vocabulary appears that this file does not name, when a named site's count moves, when a named mint's recorded checker evidence leaves its function, when a mint classified clean-kernel cites no kernel entry (or checked wrapper of one) that its function calls, or when the first-risk list rises above its ceiling.
plan: docs/plans/SELF_PROOF_EXECUTION_PLAN_2026-11-12.md (lane P; rung 2: Certified rows and Clean's release acceptance require kcheck)

how_to_read.site: one (file, enclosing symbol, token, role) group; `count` occurrences at `lines`. Derived by the scanner; never hand-edited.
how_to_read.roles: construct and call rows carry a classification; def, read, import and mention rows are pinned by count only, so a mint misread as a read cannot land unseen.
how_to_read.class: mint: a label is created from a verdict. relabel: an existing label is carried into another spelling. threshold: the label is a policy value or comparison operand. root: a checker is selected or the fenced entry is invoked.
how_to_read.checker: whose verdict the label rests on AT THE SITE. kind clean-kernel names the entry (add_decl, replay, reference, typecheck) and the theory (Extended, Lean, LeanReference, or caller-selected when the function does not build its environment). in-repo-checker: trusted Rust that is not the kernel. external-tool: a tool outside this repository. none: nothing checks at the site. inherits / not-a-mint: no verdict of its own. unexamined (Trust rows only): the census did not read behind the site and claims nothing either way; no row at trust.commit has it since the P1 review read all 16 (2026-11-12).
how_to_read.evidence_tokens: identifiers the enclosing function must keep naming in code position; when one leaves, the gate reports CHECKER MOVED and the site is re-read. A mint classified clean-kernel must also have at least one token that is a kernel entry (KERNEL_ENTRY_CALLS in the script) or a declared wrapper of one, CALLED in code position (`name(` or `name::<..>(`): a variable, field or parameter so named does not count.
how_to_read.reach: coarse, by crate and API surface: user (a shipped clean verb or public library API), trust (Trust's own code), user+trust (a Clean crate Trust links, and Trust source at the pin names the symbol or its module), internal, example, bench. It is not a call-graph proof.
how_to_read.kcheck_rung: the rung of the plan's section 6 at which the site must rest on kcheck; null with rung_note when the site mints nothing, when the label does not say kernel, or when a Trust row is unexamined.
how_to_read.entries: verbs whose acceptance is an exit status or a written artifact rather than a label. Hand-anchored to a function; the gate checks the anchor exists once in production code and still names its evidence tokens.
how_to_read.tcb: Trust rows only: what Trust's docs/TCB.md says about the site at the pinned commit, by section and line, or that it does not name it.
how_to_read.kernel_entry_wrappers: clean.kernel_entry_wrappers and trust.kernel_entry_wrappers: functions that reach a kernel entry, each with the calls it makes; the gate re-reads each body (Clean in this tree, Trust at trust.commit) and admits a wrapper only through checked hops that end at an entry, so a cycle admits nothing. trust.clean_wrappers are Clean functions that Trust sites call, read at trust.clean_pin, the Clean commit Trust builds against.

limits: The vocabulary is authority-shaped NAMES (KernelVerified, KernelChecked*, KernelProved, KernelBridged, KernelCertified, KernelAccepted, Certified, SourceVerified, the sibling tiers AxiomDependent, CertificateReplayed, AxiomDischarged, AxiomAccepted, UnsafeAccepted and clean-c-sem's StructuralProved (added 2026-11-12/13 after the P1 review), and on the Trust side KernelReferenceChecked / KernelReconstructed), WRITES to a snake_case field or local whose name says kernel_[re]verified / checked / certified / proved (`+=`, `.push/.extend/.insert/.append(`, `= true`, `: true`), and checker roots (ReferenceKernel and its entry methods, ReferenceAccepted, for_lean_replay, KernelTheory::<variant>, KernelVerifiedManifest, and Trust's certificate seam). NOT scanned, by name: clean-verify's ProofStatus::DerivedProved (1539 production occurrences in 203 files, 405 functions, measured 2026-11-12; 1516 are `proof_status:` literals in its spec tables, and its run-time promotions, three `def.proof_status = ProofStatus::DerivedProved` assignments in crates/clean-verify/src/proofs/promote.rs, are unscanned too); the generic outcome variants Verified, Proved, Checked, Accepted and Valid (277 production occurrences in 107 files, every role, measured 2026-11-12; the first census recorded 224 in 92), mostly tactic and automation outcomes; a kernel-named field assigned anything but `true`; and a write to a field whose name says checked or verified without `kernel` (`family_checked: true`). The user-facing verbs among them are the `entries`.

An environment built without a censused root runs KernelTheory::Extended. The census does not list the plain Environment::new() / with_prelude() calls (360 production calls of Environment::new at the first census), so `checker.theory = Extended` on an add_decl mint is read from the function, and `caller-selected` means the function does not decide.
A new verb that reaches the kernel through an already-counted helper is not detected; entries are hand-kept.
Scripts are out of scope: a label written by a shell or Python script is not a site here.

The Trust half is a census of one Trust commit (trust.commit). At that commit the gate is a consistency check of this file; it sees a new Trust site only when run with --trust-ref <newer ref>, which is how the pin is moved. Where no Trust checkout holds the commit the Trust half reports unknown and the gate still decides the Clean half (--require-trust makes that a failure). Trust's own tcb_document_exhaustiveness gate owns its authority table.

Trust rows marked unexamined were found by the scanner and not read through; none remains at trust.commit (the 16 there were read for the P1 review, 2026-11-12). A newly pinned Trust commit may bring new ones, named so that they cannot be mistaken for classified sites.

Classifications were made by reading each site and its enclosing function, and, for a kernel claim, the chain of functions down to a kernel entry (declared as wrappers and re-checked hop by hop). `detail` says what was read. A wrapper is matched by NAME at the citing site: the call is not resolved to the declared file and symbol, so a same-named function elsewhere would also satisfy it. A mint classified clean-kernel says the function calls a kernel entry or a checked wrapper of one; it does not say the kernel's verdict is sound, nor that every path through the function to the label reaches the call.

Routes into Clean's checkers through a third repository are held at manifest granularity (trust.links), with a hand-kept record of what was read on each route: for crates/trust-spec-temporal (ty's tla-check, linking clean-kernel and clean-ck0) the route lists the lane's acceptance sites and the theory tla-check runs (Extended), read 2026-11-12. The gate re-derives neither that list nor anything in ty; it holds the lane's kernel_rechecked writes through the site scan. A carrier crate nobody has recorded in OUTSIDE_CARRIERS is not seen.
Scope of the Clean half: crates/**/*.rs outside test targets and #[cfg(test)] items. Rust outside crates/ (scripts/crystal_a2_project, scripts/lint_*, tools under other roots) is not scanned.

The first-risk list is held by a ceiling (first_risk_limit, with first_risk_history): it falls when mints leave the list and rises only through `--write --rebase-risk '<reason>'` for a census correction that finds mints already in the tree. A correction is recorded, not checked: the reason is prose.
